entries.clue: Don’t be cruel to old comedian, simple at heart (2,4,2)

indicatorNotes.at heart: the heart of a thing is its middle, so the word for 'simple' sits in the middle of the other

blocks.note: a Goon, one of the 1950s radio comedy team (Milligan, Sellers, Secombe)
simple = easy, as in an easy task

annotation.surface: A plea for kindness towards a dim, ageing comic.
annotation.walkthrough: The Goons were a British radio comedy troupe of the 1950s, so any member is an 'old comedian'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase means treat gently, which is the opposite of being cruel, and it fits after 'Don't' in the same way.

entries.clue: Effusive person’s good conduct (6)

blocks.note: to usher is to conduct someone to their seat

annotation.surface: A remark on how a gushing type behaves well.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good conduct' reads as a noun phrase about behaviour; split it, and 'conduct' is the verb meaning to show someone the way.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: someone who gushes pours out feeling without restraint, which is what effusive means.

entries.clue: The Great Escape – film and book (6)

blocks.note: a mass departure, like the Israelites' flight from Egypt
a 1960 Otto Preminger film shares its title with the second book of the Bible

annotation.surface: A caption describing The Great Escape as both a film and a book.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics make 'The Great Escape' look like the 1963 war film; read plainly, it is the flight of the Israelites from Egypt, told in EXODUS.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the word means a great departure of people, and it names both the biblical book and the film of Leon Uris's novel.

entries.clue: Inducement to include small number in series (9)

indicatorNotes.to include: to include something is to hold it within, so the series abbreviation wraps the rest

blocks.note: ser. is the abbreviation for series

annotation.surface: A description of a sales incentive that slips a small figure into a run of offers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small number' looks like one idea, a low figure, but it is two separate words each giving its own piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a bribe or incentive offered to win someone over, the thing that makes a deal more palatable.

entries.clue: Apparently warming up, beginning to harry senior minister (6,6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: something warming up has, whimsically, come 'off ice'

annotation.surface: A political sketch: a senior minister is heating up and starting to harass someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' flags a playful reading: whatever is warming up must have been taken off the ice.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a minister holds a post in government, and anyone holding such a post is described this way.

entries.clue: Duck as light motorcycle loses one wheel? (6)

indicatorNotes.loses: whatever loses something has it taken away, so a letter drops out

blocks.note: a scooter is a light motorcycle
O is round like a wheel; one of the two Os goes

annotation.surface: Someone ducks as a scooter throws off a wheel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a verb, dodging the flying wheel; it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the scoter is a dark diving sea duck of northern coasts.

entries.clue: Weight of stone accepted in shopping basket (5)

indicatorNotes.accepted in: what is accepted in is let inside, so A goes into the basket

annotation.surface: A heavy stone has somehow been let into someone's shopping.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'stone' is also a British weight of 14 pounds, which the surface leans on; here it is a gemstone.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: the unit used for weighing gemstones, 200 milligrams.

entries.clue: Honest admitting name, sort of burglar in dock (8)

indicatorNotes.admitting: to admit is to let in, so the word for honest lets the others inside

blocks.note: a cat burglar climbs in through upper windows

annotation.surface: An honest confession in court: a cat burglar in the dock gives his name.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dock' is the courtroom dock in the surface; as the definition it is the verb, to cut short.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to dock a tail or wages is to cut it short.

entries.clue: It’s good this getting shot of a pest (8)

annotation.definition: It’s good this getting shot of a pest

blocks.note: the surface reads 'this is good'; the setter means the word that 'good' is paired with in a set farewell phrase
British slang: getting shot of means getting rid of, not shooting

annotation.surface: Relief at finally being rid of an annoying pest.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the set phrase 'good riddance!', said when something unwelcome finally leaves.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the word means the act of getting rid of something, and 'good' fronts it in the stock exclamation.

entries.clue: Leave secretly, ramp unavailable (5,3)

blocks.note: a dish that is off the menu is unavailable

annotation.surface: Someone must sneak out because the access ramp is closed.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase is British for sneaking away to avoid work or notice.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional idiom: British usage for slipping away quietly, usually to dodge something.

entries.clue: Contended resistance stops suffering from malaria (6)

indicatorNotes.stops: to stop a gap is to plug it, so R fills the middle of the other word

blocks.note: ague is malarial fever; agued = suffering from it

annotation.surface: A medical note: resistance halts the spread of malaria.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stops' looks like 'halts'; here it means fills a gap, as a stopper does.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to contend a point is to maintain it in debate.

entries.clue: Doubt the gospel? (8,4)

blocks.note: read as a noun, the symbol that stands for uncertainty; read as a verb, to query or challenge
one of the four gospels, named after its evangelist, here the object of the verb; the clue's final punctuation is itself a hint

annotation.surface: A sceptic's challenge to scripture.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, it asks you to question Mark; read as a phrase, the answer is the punctuation that stands for doubt, and it ends the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: we say a doubt hangs over something as this symbol does, and the instruction reading is literal.

entries.clue: Go up: temperature perfect for returning (5)

indicatorNotes.returning: something returning goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: The perfect temperature for going back up.
annotation.walkthrough: The colon suggests a heading and its explanation; really 'Go up' is the definition and everything after it builds one string that is then turned around.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a volcano that blows its top goes up, as does anything that explodes.

entries.clue: Great area on Earth’s exterior in which woodlice are found (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, putting one thing on another means adding it after, so ACE and A follow

blocks.note: the Earth's crust is its outer layer

annotation.surface: A nature note about a vast region of the Earth's surface where woodlice live.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great area' seems to be a big region; it splits into two pieces. Woodlice are land-living relatives of crabs.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the zoological class takes in woodlice along with crabs, lobsters and shrimps.

entries.clue: Intuit a chess blunder, making up for it (12)

indicatorNotes.blunder: a blunder throws things into disorder, so the letters get muddled

annotation.surface: A chess player senses a blunder and presses on to make up for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Making up for it' reads as compensating; split it, and 'up for it' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal idiom: someone up for it is keen and eager to take part.

entries.clue: What noon means to some people: time correction (9)

blocks.note: noon is the end of the morning: AM END

annotation.surface: A curious question of what midday signifies to certain people, followed by a clock adjustment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To' seems to belong to the question about meaning; it only joins the first two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a change made to put a text or law right.

entries.clue: Coming in last, contrary to expectations (5,3)

blocks.note: the last finisher arrives behind every other runner
said of an outcome that happens despite predictions, as in 'it rained ___'

annotation.surface: A runner finishes last, to everyone's surprise.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal: whoever comes in last arrives after all the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: literally behind everyone else, and idiomatically in spite of what was expected.

entries.clue: Batters liable to be caught in the bar (8)

blocks.note: in cricket, a batter who takes a thin edge off the ball often gets caught behind
a chocolate bar with peanuts and caramel

annotation.surface: Drunken brawlers likely to be arrested in the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Batters' and 'bar' suggest fighting in a pub; in cricket a snick is a thin edge off the bat, which often carries to a fielder.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: people who snick the ball, and the brand name of a well-known chocolate bar.

entries.clue: Resentful air spoiled farewell observances (7,5)

indicatorNotes.spoiled: something spoiled is ruined, and ruined letters fall into a new order

annotation.surface: A bitter mood ruined the goodbye ceremonies.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a family row at a send-off, and the answer is that very occasion.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the ceremonies that mark a last goodbye to the dead.

entries.clue: Drawer twice the size of another (6)

annotation.definition: Drawer twice the size of another

blocks.note: not a drawer in a chest but one who draws: a drawing instrument
measured in letters: six against the three of another writing instrument whose name it begins with

annotation.surface: A chest of drawers with one drawer double the size of its neighbour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like furniture; it is something that draws. PENCIL has six letters, twice the three of PEN, and starts with it.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: 'drawer' as anything that draws, here the most common drawing tool.

entries.clue: Highest standards of ladies’ dancing (6)

indicatorNotes.dancing: dancers move about and change places, as the letters do

annotation.surface: A judge's remark on the top marks in women's dance.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive apostrophe is ignored; only the six letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the perfect standards one aims at but seldom reaches.

entries.clue: Such mathematics left audience floundering (9)

indicatorNotes.floundering: to flounder is to thrash about clumsily, so the letters tumble into a new order

annotation.surface: A lecture on mathematics left the listeners out of their depth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' is not the verb of the sentence; it is a single letter, added to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: 'such' points to a kind of mathematics, here the classical geometry of Euclid.

entries.clue: Suffer, beyond medical help, disabled (5)

indicatorNotes.disabled: read as dis-ABLE-d: the word is made to lose ABLE

annotation.surface: A patient suffering, disabled and past saving.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disabled' is split as a working instruction rather than read as a description.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: one suffers or brings on a loss, a penalty or a cost.

entries.clue: Be terrified of judge’s pronouncement (5)

indicatorNotes.pronouncement: a pronouncement is spoken, so the name is heard rather than spelt

annotation.surface: Fearing the verdict a judge will deliver.
annotation.walkthrough: Judge Dredd is the lawman of the British comic 2000 AD. A judge's 'pronouncement' naturally suggests a ruling, not a name said out loud.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to fear something greatly, looking ahead to it with terror.

entries.clue: Homeland Security for one get on closing clubs in E Coast city (6)

indicatorNotes.closing: the city part comes last, closing off the word
indicatorNotes.in: clubs are put in the city, so the letter goes inside its abbreviation

blocks.note: to get on in years is to age

annotation.surface: A US security department growing old while shutting down clubs in New York.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get on' means grow older here, not board or make progress.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the US Department of Homeland Security is one government body of this kind.

entries.clue: In depresssed area knight spies city (8)

blocks.note: a vale is a valley, a depression in the land

annotation.surface: A knight in a valley catches sight of a city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spies' looks like a verb, sees; it is a noun. A 'depressed area' sounds economic but is a dip in the ground.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a port city on Spain's east coast, the country's third largest.

entries.clue: They are beaten less, or flogged (6)

indicatorNotes.flogged: something flogged is knocked about, and so are the letters

annotation.surface: A grim choice about punishment: beaten less, or flogged.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' and 'flogged' both suggest punishment; 'beaten' is the definition in its sporting sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: those defeated in a contest, beaten in the sporting sense.

entries.clue: Game that looks easy for beginners in brief sketches (8)

indicatorNotes.for beginners: the beginners of words are their first letters
indicatorNotes.in: the gathered letters are put in the sketches, inside the word

blocks.note: first letters of that, looks, easy

annotation.surface: A game said to look simple for newcomers, shown in short sketches.
annotation.walkthrough: Skittles is a British pub game of bowling a ball at wooden pins. 'Beginners' seems to mean novices; it asks for first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a traditional pub game in which a ball is rolled to knock down pins.
